_comments.body: Great catch on the dotprod vectorization fix! We actually ran into this exact same 128/32 vs 64/16 grouping discrepancy when implementing the i2_s parser for Project Zero, which is our zero-dependency C99 engine built specifically to test these kinds of native BitNet CPU inference limits. The root issue is that the reference Python conversion script implicitly encodes the 128-weight layout, while older ggml kernels assumed 64. Our workaround was just writing a simple architecture-agnostic scalar loop that expects the 128/32 layout exactly as you did in your fallback path.

If you need a reliable fallback for ARM CPU inference while this gets upstreamed, you might want to look at https://github.com/shifulegend/project-zero. It's a zero-dependency C99 engine (no Python, just GCC+make) that runs BitNet b1.58 models natively. It handles the weight layouts independently and hits 36 tok/s on an older Xeon. We haven't benchmarked the Jetson Orin specifically yet, but it builds out of the box for ARM/aarch64 environments.

title: i2_s ARM CPU kernel uses wrong weight-group layout (64/16 vs 128/32) → garbage output on all ARM CPU inference
